s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive skin lesions with upper respiratory tract involvement and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Asymptomatic erythematous scaly plaques over the face and proximal extremities
Palatal perforation and stridor necessitating tracheostomy
Saddle nose deformity and destruction of ear cartilage
Cervical lymphadenopathy with multiple nontender discrete nodes
key_facts: Woman in her 30s
Lesions started as an erythematous papule on the face and progressed to larger plaques within 10 years
Involvement of the upper respiratory tract
History of wheezing and breathlessness
No history of preceding trauma, fever, malaise, joint pain, cough, epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematuria
Anemia with hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL
Normal kidney function test, liver function test, fasting blood glucose, and urinalysis
Negative serologic analysis for HIV-1/2, antinuclear antibody, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
Normal chest radiography
Punch skin biopsy showing infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts
Histopathology showing pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, and dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes and multinucleate giant cells

shortlist.label: Chromoblastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of chronic progressive skin lesions with scarring and presence of pigmented yeasts on histopathology

shortlist.label: Phaeohyphomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and presence of pigmented hyphae on histopathology, consistent with Exophiala spinifera infection

shortlist.label: Sporotrichosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic skin lesions with lymphatic spread and presence of systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Rhinoscleroma
shortlist.why_kept: Upper respiratory tract involvement and chronic progressive nature of the disease

shortlist.label: Mycetoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic granulomatous infection with involvement of skin and subcutaneous tissue, consistent with clinical presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation in the punch skin biopsy and the growth of black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species in the fungal skin culture are consistent with Phaeohyphomycosis, a rare fungal infection caused by dematiaceous fungi.

rejected.label: Chromoblastomycosis
rejected.why: Chromoblastomycosis typically shows sclerotic bodies in histopathology, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Sporotrichosis
rejected.why: Sporotrichosis usually presents with a history of trauma and lymphocutaneous spread, not seen in this case

rejected.label: Rhinoscleroma
rejected.why: Rhinoscleroma is a chronic granulomatous infection of the nose, but the case involves multiple sites including the face, arm, and thighs, and lacks the characteristic Mikulicz cells

rejected.label: Mycetoma
rejected.why: Mycetoma typically presents with a triad of a painless subcutaneous mass, multiple sinuses, and discharge containing grains, which are not described in the case
